approach: Add two optional keys, `planner_revision_model` and `planner_revision_effort`, to `Models` in config.rs. A new `Models::planner_revision_setting(model, effort)` uses each key only when it is set and not weaker than the current planner value. Effort is ranked by index in `EFFORT_LEVELS`. The model is ranked by index in `producer_allowed`, whose doc comment now says "weakest first". A part that would lower the value, or cannot be ranked, is ignored on its own. In `planning_round` a call is a revision call when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. That covers a critic revise and a mechanical plan-rule revision. Round 1 and a seeded first call are unchanged. A revision call takes its model from the new function and sets `spec.effort` after `agent_spec`, as producer.rs:338 does. The UI line shows the effort, and the invocation record carries both values. The `planner_revision_model` membership check runs after the OLY-B-SET-02 family loop, so the existing family tests keep their errors. `reading_inputs` clears both keys like `job_plan`. `producer_setting` and `hard_producer_*` are not read on the planner path. The effect in this repo, stated in athena.toml, the CHANGELOG, D179 and spec, covers both planned cases: a hard reading (sonnet/high to sonnet/xhigh, effort only) and an unmarked reading planned because it asks for a fails-without run (reader's pick, haiku or sonnet, at high to sonnet/xhigh, so a haiku planner moves up to sonnet).

decisions.choice: Dedicated keys planner_revision_model and planner_revision_effort, never derived from hard_producer_*.
decisions.reason: hard_producer_model is claude-sonnet-5-5 and hard_producer_effort is high (athena.toml:25-26). A hard job's planner already runs on that model at verifier_effort high (athena.toml:21; effort_for maps Planner to verifier_effort, config.rs ~835). Reusing hard_producer_* would change nothing for a hard reading and could lower the setting in another config. Dedicated keys do apply to a second planned case, which answers finding 1. run/mod.rs:1087-1092 plans in hard mode when `reading.hard_reason.is_some() || asks_for_fails_without_run(&reading)`. job_plan.rs:1232-1249 confirms that an unmarked reading is planned this way. For such a reading reading.rs:869-871 uses producer_setting(.., false), so the planner runs on the reader's pick from producer_allowed = [haiku, sonnet] (athena.toml:14) at high. Effective setting in this repo, by planned case. (1) Hard reading: today sonnet/high every round; with the change, round 1 is sonnet/high and each revision call is sonnet/xhigh (effort only). (2) Unmarked reading planned for a fails-without criterion: today (reader's model, high) every round. With a haiku pick, round 1 is haiku/high and revision calls are sonnet/xhigh (model and effort rise). With a sonnet pick, revision calls are sonnet/xhigh (effort only).

rejected.option: Reuse hard_producer_model and hard_producer_effort via producer_setting
rejected.why: No effect for a hard reading, it can lower the planner setting, and the request forbids it.

rejected.option: A code-side bump of effort by one level on revision
rejected.why: It hides the rule from athena.toml and gives the owner no value to set.

decisions.choice: Judge 'not weaker' in code: effort by index in EFFORT_LEVELS (config.rs:336-337), model by index in producer_allowed read as weakest first. A part that would lower the value, or cannot be ranked, is ignored on its own. The 'weakest first' contract is written on the producer_allowed field's own doc comment (config.rs:317), on both new fields, and in a comment above producer_allowed in athena.toml.
decisions.reason: The rule is enforced by mechanism and tested. Answers finding 4: config.rs:317 has no order contract today, so the plan adds one where a later editor of the list will see it. A config.rs table row with producer_allowed reversed to [sonnet, haiku] pins behavior under reordering.

rejected.option: Ignore both keys together when either would lower the setting
rejected.why: The reading says only that part falls back.

rejected.option: Hard-code a family order haiku < sonnet < opus
rejected.why: Brittle on version bumps; the allowed list already carries the order.

decisions.reason: It is exactly a call after a critic revise (round advances in plan_round, planning.rs:41) or after a mechanical revision (passes counted, planning.rs:68-70). A seeded first call has `revision` Some but is neither.

A config.rs table row with a reversed list pins the behavior, and a test pins REPO_CONFIG order (haiku before sonnet).

risks.risk: The effect in this repo is narrower than 'always a model change'. A hard reading's planner already runs on sonnet, so only effort rises (high to xhigh). risks.mitigation: Caps are unchanged and raising them is out of scope. A timeout stops planning with the existing reason. The change is reversible by deleting two keys.

demonstrations.method: Scripted job with [job_plan] on and max_rounds 3. The reader output is overridden so the ordinary planner model is claude-haiku-5-5. Planner queue `[good_plan()]`, critic queue `[revising_critique(), accepting_critique()]`. A wrapper around `planning_script` records (role, spec.model, spec.effort) per call. The test also reads the job's Planner invocation records and the `Lines` UI.
demonstrations.observes: Planner call 1 records claude-haiku-5-5 and high, with UI line `planner    claude-haiku-5-5 · high · …`. Planner call 2, after the critic revise, records claude-sonnet-5-5 and xhigh, with the matching UI line. Critic calls keep their own model and effort. The job lands.
demonstrations.fails_without: With planning.rs unchanged, call 2 records the ordinary model and high, so the call-2 record and UI-line assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Three tests on the same seam. (a) Mechanical: planner queue `[bad_plan(), good_plan()]`, critic accepts. (b) Weaker keys: reader's producer_model overridden to claude-sonnet-5-5, as `run_planned_behavior` mutates the reader output. Pair 1 is model haiku with effort medium. Pair 2 is model haiku with effort xhigh. The critic revises. (c) Both keys unset: planner queue `[bad_plan(), good_plan()]` and a revising critic over 3 rounds.
demonstrations.observes: (a) Planner calls are (ordinary, high) then (sonnet, xhigh), with no critic call between them. (b) Pair 1: every planner call stays (sonnet, high). Pair 2: revision calls are (sonnet, xhigh), so only the effort part applies. (c) Every planner call across the mechanical pass and all 3 rounds is the same (ordinary, high).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the mechanical-pass condition, (a) records the ordinary setting on call 2. Without the no-weaker rule, (b) records (haiku, medium) on revision calls. Without the unset fallback, (c) fails when any call differs.

demonstrations.method: The core test of criterion 1 asserts the UI line `planner    <model> · <effort> · …` on round 1 and on the revision round, and the invocation records. The drain.rs test parses `common::test_config()` (athena.toml minus job_plan) with `Config::parse`. It asserts `planner_revision_setting("claude-sonnet-5-5", "high")` is (claude-sonnet-5-5, xhigh), and `planner_revision_setting("claude-haiku-5-5", "high")` is also (claude-sonnet-5-5, xhigh). The "high" is `effort_for(Role::Planner)` of that config. Also run `cargo test -p athena-core a_critic_revise_sends_the_next_planner_call_at_the_revision_model_and_effort`.
demonstrations.observes: The repo's own athena.toml gives a revision call sonnet/xhigh for both planned cases. A hard reading differs from round 1 in effort only. An unmarked reading planned for a fails-without criterion and picking haiku differs in model and effort. The core test shows the owner-visible line and the record per round.
demonstrations.fails_without: If athena.toml lacked the entry or it were weaker, the drain.rs test fails. Without the effort in the planner line, the core test's line assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: drain.rs calls production `Config::parse` and `Models::planner_revision_setting` on the `test_config()` string (tests/common/mod.rs:19-45); no agent needed. The core test uses `Athena::go` and `Lines`. Step 8 adds the drain test.

demonstrations.method: Read the diffs. `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain planner_revision` and `cargo test -p athena-data planner_revision` parse the real athena.toml entry.
demonstrations.observes: athena.toml [models] has `planner_revision_model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` and `planner_revision_effort = "xhigh"`. Its comment names the keys without `key = ` text and says producer_allowed is weakest first and a key earlier in the list than the current model is ignored. The CHANGELOG [Unreleased] ### Added entry states both planned cases. Hard reading: today sonnet/high every round; with the change round 1 is sonnet/high and each revision call is sonnet/xhigh, effort only. Unmarked reading planned for a fails-without criterion: today the reader's model (haiku or sonnet) at high every round; with the change a haiku planner's revision calls run sonnet/xhigh and a sonnet planner's run sonnet/xhigh. It says round 1 and a seeded first call are unchanged, what the keys do, and that `planner_usd` is unchanged. The OLY-A-11 mechanism text in docs/spec.toml names the revision setting.

One new entry D179 appended after D178 in the D136 field shape. Its Provenance bullet records why dedicated keys replace hard_producer_* (no effect on a hard reading, possible lowering, earlier job 20261113-194336-scfc) and the two planned cases. The diff shows additions only.

demonstrations.method: Three separate simple commands on the final tree, each its own command: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --locked`. None is chained with another. The Athena-recorded passing checks fmt, clippy and test on the final tree may be cited instead.
demonstrations.observes: fmt clean, clippy without warnings, all crates pass, including config.rs tests, run/tests.rs, drain.rs, `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` and `model_roster`.
demonstrations.fails_without: A compile error, a clippy warning or a stale expectation of the planner line fails the matching check.
